mustFix.title: Both authority-boundary EE slots carry the range 'EE-1 through EE-6a' in place of the exact seven-class enumeration; the range sweeps in EE-3a, whose leftover-design remains open and is not G29's.
mustFix.text: The draft's two 'Does not reopen leftover-design' slots read 'EE-1 through EE-6a'. The set D-157 actually closed as remainder G29 execution is exactly seven classes: EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b, EE-6a. That same seven-member enumeration appears verbatim in D-157's decision text, in file 08's DR-G29 row, in the recorded artifact's namedClassesThisGate, in the recorded artifact's own binding doesNot limb, and in D-204 — the direct G29 predecessor COORD entry, whose adversarial review tested precisely this and required set-and-order identity across all four sources. The range is not that set. The live EE namespace, enumerated across COORD, file 08, and the G29 artifacts, contains EE-3a sitting between EE-2 and EE-3b, so 'EE-1 through EE-6a' denotes at minimum an eighth class, and additionally implies EE-3, EE-5, and EE-6, none of which exist anywhere in the corpus. EE-3a is not an idle name: D-156 records the DR-117 leftover-design grouping for ten classes and states expressly that 'EE-3a and EE-6b/EE-7c/EE-7e standing from D-155 is not retargeted', and D-156 scopes that cluster at G09/G14/G16, not G29. The sentence 'does not reopen leftover-design of X' presupposes that X's leftover-design is closed; EE-3a's is recorded as remaining open and held apart at other gates. So the range makes a G29 leftover-remasurement entry (a) misrecite the scope of an adopted decision, D-157, (b) carry a false presupposition about a class D-156 and D-155 hold open, and (c) reach across gates on an identifier its own Measured inputs table establishes nothing about. The draft's own line 140 asserts that this entry 'does not invent identifiers', which the range contradicts on its face.
mustFix.whyNotStylistic: The range form appears nowhere in any adopted COORD entry — D-155, D-156, D-157, D-204, and the two further COORD sites all enumerate. It appears in the recorded artifact only in the descriptive registerRowNote and purpose prose; the artifact's binding doesNot limb enumerates. The draft therefore promoted loose prose shorthand into the COORD entry's authority-boundary limb, which is the durable authoritative record, and did so in the one slot where the exact set governs. A defensive reading — that 'through' ranges over D-157's own seven-member sequence and so excludes EE-3a — is available, but an authority-boundary sentence that admits two readings, one of which misstates two adopted decisions, is not adequate for adoption. The ambiguity is itself the defect.
mustFix.notCharged: This is not charged as a takeover of G21, G23, G24, or G30; none of those is touched. It is not charged as an authority grab; the sentence is a disclaimer and grants nothing. It is charged as a false-or-ambiguous recital in the limb that defines the entry's boundary.
mustFix.fix: In both slots, replace 'EE-1 through EE-6a' with the exact enumeration already used by D-157, file 08, D-204, and the recorded artifact's doesNot limb: 'EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b, or EE-6a'. No other change is required and no other limb is affected.

decision: OBJECT - 1 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. The subject is unmoved at a91add3e... mode 0444, HEAD is the D-253 adoption commit itself, and all ten cited digests recompute exactly. Both Stage A verdict files were opened and independently confirm ACCEPT 0/0 with the observation dispositions recited accurately, including the single unlabeled non-charged disclosure in the Claude file. Twenty-five of twenty-six attacks are refuted against live bytes: the draft-time currency of leftover-join.v3 is stated correctly in all four places it appears, leftoverDesign is recited as [OBL-G29-FX-AUTHORING] matching the artifact, occupancy v3 is current and v2 is labelled not current, the no-cell-edit branch enumerates D-237 through D-253 without ever touching D-236, the identifier is unoccupied, file 08 and required-now 28 are untouched, and the entry expressly does not claim that D-056 gates 2 and 3 fail. One attack lands. Both of the entry's authority-boundary slots read 'Does not reopen leftover-design of EE-1 through EE-6a' where D-157, file 08's DR-G29 row, D-204, and the recorded artifact's own binding doesNot limb all enumerate exactly seven classes: EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b, EE-6a. EE-3a exists in the live namespace between EE-2 and EE-3b, D-156 records its standing from D-155 as expressly not retargeted and scoped at G09/G14/G16, and its leftover-design remains open. The range therefore misrecites what D-157 closed, presupposes closure of a class the corpus holds open, and reaches across gates on an identifier this draft measures nothing about, while the draft's own line 140 asserts it invents no identifiers. The range appears in the recorded artifact only in descriptive prose, never in its binding limb, and in no adopted COORD entry at all. The fix is mechanical: restore the seven-class enumeration in both slots. Nothing else in the draft requires change.
